findings.finding: The node now has no open questions, records decided design decisions, includes implementation notes, and has completed design tasks.
The chosen reusable layer is composition-first and does not require a heavyweight shared widget base class.
The first helper set is explicitly defined as owned timers, owned subscriptions, owned workers, and owned auxiliary IPC lanes, matching the current repeated ownership problems.
The design keeps lane, timer, and subscription failures local to the owning widget rather than flattening them into daemon-wide disconnect semantics.
The helper layer preserves the async-callable/partial worker scheduling convention and composes with parent-screen ownership of the shared control bridge.
